source_meta._title: Adding effects with an effects_changed advancement causes a packet error (ConcurrentModificationException) if it was triggered by Milk

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a fresh vanilla singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled so the required item and initial status effect can be obtained deterministically. Install the supplied effect-bug-1.zip data pack before creating the world. Do not test in fix version 24w34a.
preconditions: Use the exact Java Edition release 1.21 listed as affected by the report.
Have the report attachment effect-bug-1.zip available as a local file.
Use a fresh world so the supplied advancement has no completion state left over from an earlier test.
Enable commands/cheats; Creative mode is selected only to simplify deterministic setup and is not stated as a bug requirement.
Keep effect-bug-1.zip enabled throughout the reproduction.
The player must have at least one active status effect immediately before drinking the milk.
Clear the effect specifically by finishing consumption of a milk bucket. Do not substitute /effect clear, because the report states that command clearing does not reproduce the issue.
No additional players are required. The report indicates the issue can occur in singleplayer through the integrated server as well as on a dedicated server.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an unmodified Java Edition installation for the exact release 1.21, launch it, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left area of the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.21, with no snapshot or fix-version identifier such as 24w34a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select Create New World, give the world any name, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands/cheats are allowed. Creative mode and commands are setup conveniences rather than report-required gameplay conditions.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open for a new Creative world in which commands will be available.

steps.action: On the world-creation screen, open the More tab, select Data Packs, and select Open Pack Folder. Copy the supplied effect-bug-1.zip file into the folder that opens. Leave the archive as a .zip file; do not rename or reconstruct its contents.
steps.success_cue: After returning to Minecraft, an available data-pack entry corresponding to effect-bug-1.zip is visible on the Data Packs screen.

steps.action: Enable the effect-bug-1.zip entry by clicking its arrow so it moves from Available to Selected. Select Done, then select Create New World. If the file does not appear or cannot be enabled, stop rather than replacing it with a different data pack.
steps.success_cue: World creation begins with the effect-bug-1.zip entry in the selected/enabled data-pack list.

steps.action: Wait for the new world and integrated server to finish loading. Do not start the test while the loading screen is displayed.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the world, surrounding chunks are rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Verify that the supplied data pack is enabled. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat prints the enabled data-pack list and includes a file entry corresponding to effect-bug-1.zip. The command does not report an unknown-command, permission, or data-pack loading error.

steps.action: Obtain one milk bucket before applying the test effect. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback states that a milk bucket was given, and a Milk Bucket is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: If the Milk Bucket is not already in one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the screen, press E to open the inventory, move the Milk Bucket into any hotbar slot, and close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: A Milk Bucket icon is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots after the inventory is closed.

steps.action: Give the player a temporary, visible status effect. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. This uses Speed I for 120 seconds as the report permits any effect. Do not use /effect clear afterward.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that Speed was applied to the player, and an active status-effect icon is visible.

steps.action: Confirm the milk precondition without clearing anything: press E to open the inventory, verify that at least one active status effect is listed, then close the inventory. Proceed promptly enough that the temporary Speed effect has not expired.
steps.success_cue: The inventory has been closed and the player still has at least one active status effect immediately before selecting the milk.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Milk Bucket by pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling until that slot is outlined. Do not drink it yet.
steps.success_cue: The Milk Bucket is displayed in the player's hand and its hotbar slot has the active-slot outline.

steps.action: Drink the selected Milk Bucket: press and continuously hold the Use Item control, which is right mouse button by default, until the drinking animation finishes. Do not release the control early, switch slots, run /effect clear, or perform another action during consumption.
steps.exact_input: Hold right-click until milk consumption completes
steps.success_cue: The drinking animation has completed and the held Milk Bucket has become an empty Bucket. Immediately stop input and hand control to the observation subsystem.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just finished consuming the milk, the milk bucket has changed into an empty bucket, and no further command or player action has been performed. Begin observing the client connection and integrated-server state immediately.
uncertainties: The supplied report names effect-bug-1.zip but does not include the archive's internal files, namespace, advancement identifier, pack description, or any data-pack-generated confirmation message. The plan therefore verifies the attachment by its enabled file entry rather than by an unknown internal identifier.
The report does not require a particular game mode. Creative mode and commands are used only as a deterministic way to acquire milk and apply an initial effect.

The report states that the issue occurs in server handling and distinguishes singleplayer from non-singleplayer behavior, but it does not require a dedicated server. This plan chooses the simpler fresh singleplayer/integrated-server path.

The exact display label of the enabled data pack may differ from the attachment filename because a data pack can define its own description. The enabled entry must nevertheless correspond to effect-bug-1.zip.

External verification was used only for operational data-pack installation, reload/list behavior, Java /effect syntax, and milk's effect-clearing mechanic; it was not used to replace the report's reproduction sequence.
